DDInter602.mechanism: Coadministration with inhibitors of CYP450 3A4 may increase the plasma concentrations of dronedarone, which is primarily metabolized by the isoenzyme. Data are not available for dronedarone in combination with other, less potent CYP450 3A4 inhibitors.

DDInter612.mechanism: Coadministration with inhibitors of CYP450 3A4 may increase the plasma concentrations of duvelisib, which is primarily metabolized by the isoenzyme.

DDInter625.mechanism: Coadministration with inhibitors of the OATP 1B1 hepatic uptake transporter, CYP450 3A4 metabolic isoenzyme, and/or P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter may increase the plasma concentrations of elagolix. The effect of P-gp inhibitors on the pharmacokinetics of elagolix has not been studied, but some increases in elagolix exposure may occur, as it is a P-gp substrate. Increased exposure to elagolix may increase the risk of serious adverse effects such as bone loss, suicidal ideation and behavior, exacerbation of mood disorders, and hepatic transaminase elevations.

DDInter629.mechanism: Coadministration with weak inhibitors of CYP450 3A4 may increase the plasma concentrations of eliglustat, which is primarily metabolized by CYP450 2D6 and, to a lesser extent, CYP450 3A4. DDInter704.mechanism: Coadministration with inhibitors of CYP450 3A4 and/or P-glycoprotein may increase the blood concentrations of everolimus following oral administration. DDInter731.mechanism: Coadministration with inhibitors of CYP450 3A4 may increase the plasma concentrations of fesoterodine's active metabolite, 5-hydroxymethyl tolterodine, which is partially metabolized by the isoenzyme. The possibility of prolonged and/or increased pharmacologic effects of fesoterodine should be considered. Because 5-hydroxymethyl tolterodine is also metabolized by CYP450 2D6, the clinical significance of the interaction may be greater in patients who are CYP450 2D6-deficient, or so-called poor metabolizers of CYP450 2D6 (approximately 7% of Caucasians and less than 2% of Asians and individuals of African descent) who may rely more on the 3A4 metabolic pathway for clearance of the drug.

DDInter741.mechanism: Coadministration with weak inhibitors of CYP450 3A4 may increase the plasma concentrations of flibanserin, which is primarily metabolized by CYP450 3A4 and, to a lesser extent, by CYP450 2C19.

DDInter817.mechanism: Coadministration with inhibitors of CYP450 3A4 and/or P-glycoprotein (P-gp) may increase the plasma concentrations of gilteritinib, which is a substrate of both the isoenzyme and the efflux transporter.

DDInter822.mechanism: Coadministration with inhibitors of CYP450 3A4 may increase the plasma concentrations of glasdegib, which is primarily metabolized by the isoenzyme.

DDInter841.mechanism: Coadministration with inhibitors of CYP450 3A4 may increase the plasma concentrations of grazoprevir, which is a substrate of the isoenzyme.

DDInter855.mechanism: Coadministration with drugs that are capable of increasing the activity of delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase (e.g., estrogens, barbiturates, steroid metabolites, rifampin) may negate the pharmacologic effect of hemin.
